human_feedback_verbatim:
You are still taking too much unnecessary damage in combat. When enemies are attacking and lethal is not available, first calculate the incoming damage and how much of it can be prevented with the block currently available in your hand. If playing defensive cards can substantially reduce or completely prevent the damage, prioritize that defense unless spending the energy on damage will clearly end the fight or remove a major threat. Do not take preventable HP loss just to deal a small amount of extra damage. At the same time, when enemies are not attacking, do not waste energy on unnecessary block and use the turn to deal damage, set up your deck, or apply useful debuffs.

You also need to continue following encounter-specific strategies that were taught in previous runs rather than treating newer lessons as replacements. For example, against Centurion and Mystic, prioritize killing Centurion before Mystic as previously taught. More generally, consider which enemy is the main threat and follow previously learned target priorities instead of choosing targets only based on immediate damage. Continue sequencing cards correctly as well: apply effects such as Vulnerable before attacks that benefit from them, and play according to the synergies and strengths of the deck you have built.

Your deck is also becoming too large because you are still taking cards that are only individually useful rather than necessary for the build. Commit to the deck's existing strategy and be much more selective with card rewards. Once the deck already has a functioning damage plan, defense, draw/energy and supporting synergy, Skip should be the default unless a new card clearly fills an important missing role or significantly strengthens the existing build. Do not keep adding cards simply because they are decent cards. Avoid unnecessary redundancy and deck dilution, and keep the deck compact enough that its strongest cards and synergies are drawn consistently.
